newsitem.title: CHINA: LUJIAZUI OPENS LIMIT-DOWN ON RESULTS.
newsitem.headline: LUJIAZUI OPENS LIMIT-DOWN ON RESULTS.

text.p: Hard currency B shares in Shanghai Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone Development Co Ltd opened 10 percent limit-down at $1.188 on Monday afternoon after the firm posted poor 1997 interim results, brokers said.
Trading in the firm's shares was suspended in the morning for the results announcement.

The real estate firm, a key B share firm with heavy weighting on Shanghai's B share index, posted net profit of 179.376 million yuan for the first half of 1997, sharply down from 548.959 million in the first half of 1996, a company statement issued after Friday's session said.

"The results were completely out of investor expectations," said one trader. "In consideration of the high price of the company's shares, panic selling emerged right after trading in the shares resumed."
Analysts hold different views about the results.
"The poor results in the first half cannot represent the prospects for the whole of 1997 or the next few years," said one Shanghai-based foreign broker.
"The firm's land banks are holding their value because Pudong is developing quickly, and this will help improve the firm's second-half (1997) performance," he said.
"Shanghai's real estate market is still weak," said an investment analyst with a major Chinese securities house.
"If there is no major positive news to help boost the market, the company will face difficulties in selling land and other property as well," he said.
